description: `detectRegistryStatusDrift`, documented in verification-architecture.md as a REQ-002/REQ-004 'pure core' primitive meant to be independently unit-testable (REQ-006), does NOT itself fail-closed when its own `canonicalRegistry` argument is null/unobservable: `flattenRegistrySlotStatus(canonicalRegistry)` on a null input returns `{}` (config-drift.mjs:113-115: `if (!slots || typeof slots !== 'object') return {}`), which the function then silently treats as a canonical registry with zero declared slots -- every present slot in every copy would be reported as a spurious `declared: undefined` drift rather than the `reason: 'unobservable'` FAIL REQ-004 requires. The ONLY place this is actually guarded is the composed wrapper `runConfigDriftDetector` (config-drift.mjs:420-423: `classifyObservability(canonicalRegistry) === 'UNOBSERVABLE' ? ... : detectRegistryStatusDrift(...)`), which currently masks the gap in production. But per REQ-006's own stated purpose (independently testable pure primitive), and since this function is directly exported and directly imported by config-drift.test.mjs, a caller invoking `detectRegistryStatusDrift` directly with a null canonicalRegistry (exactly the kind of unit-level fixture PROP-009/PROP-010 already exercise for the per-copy case) gets silently-wrong output, not a fail-closed FAIL. No test anywhere calls `detectRegistryStatusDrift(null, copies)` or `detectRegistryStatusDrift(undefined, copies)` directly -- only the copy-level null case (`registryOrNull: null`) is tested at this layer; the canonical-level null case is only tested one level up, through the wrapper.
requiredFix: Add the same `classifyObservability(canonicalRegistry) === 'UNOBSERVABLE'` guard inside `detectRegistryStatusDrift` itself (returning an unobservable FAIL per copy) so the pure primitive is correct in isolation, not just when called through the one wrapper that happens to guard it externally. Add a direct unit test for `detectRegistryStatusDrift(null, copies)`.
